plain_text:
RSV is a highly contagious common respiratory virus. People of any
age can get infected. It usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms.
semantic_text: RSV is a highly contagious common respiratory virus. People of any age can get infected. It usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms.

plain_text:
RSV spreads from person to person directly, such as kissing the
face of a child who has RSV, or indirectly, such as through the air by
coughing and sneezing. You can also catch it by touching an object or
surface with the virus on it before touching your mouth, nose, or eyes.
semantic_text: RSV spreads from person to person directly, such as kissing the face of a child who has RSV, or indirectly, such as through the air by coughing and sneezing. You can also catch it by touching an object or surface with the virus on it before touching your mouth, nose, or eyes.

plain_text:
In the United States, RSV infections usually occur from fall through
spring. People with RSV are generally contagious for three to eight
days. But sometimes infants and people with weakened immune
systems can continue to spread the virus for as long as four weeks.
semantic_text: In the United States, RSV infections usually occur from fall through spring. People with RSV are generally contagious for three to eight days. But sometimes infants and people with weakened immune systems can continue to spread the virus for as long as four weeks.

plain_text:
While most cases are mild, it can cause serious lung infections in
certain groups at higher risk, including:
semantic_text: While most cases are mild, it can cause serious lung infections in certain groups at higher risk, including:

plain_text:
■ Infants
■ Older adults, especially those ages 65 and older
■ People with chronic medical conditions such as heart
or lung disease
■ People with weakened immune systems
semantic_text: ■ Infants ■ Older adults, especially those ages 65 and older ■ People with chronic medical conditions such as heart or lung disease ■ People with weakened immune systems

plain_text:
Symptoms of RSV infection usually start about four to
six days after infection and may mimic the common cold:
semantic_text: Symptoms of RSV infection usually start about four to six days after infection and may mimic the common cold:

plain_text:
■ Runny nose
■ Decrease in appetite
■ Cough
■ Sneezing
■ Fever
■ Wheezing
■ Trouble breathing
semantic_text: ■ Runny nose ■ Decrease in appetite ■ Cough ■ Sneezing ■ Fever ■ Wheezing ■ Trouble breathing

plain_text:
RSV can survive for many hours
on hard surfaces, such as tables and
crib rails. It typically lives on soft
surfaces, such as tissues and hands,
for shorter amounts of time.
semantic_text: RSV can survive for many hours on hard surfaces, such as tables and crib rails. It typically lives on soft surfaces, such as tissues and hands, for shorter amounts of time.

plain_text:
These symptoms usually appear in stages instead of all at once.
In very young infants, the only symptoms may be irritability,
decreased activity, and trouble breathing. RSV can also cause
more severe infections, especially in people at high risk. These
infections include bronchiolitis, an inflammation of the small
airways in the lung, and pneumonia, an infection of the lungs.
If symptoms get worse over time, see a doctor right away.
semantic_text: These symptoms usually appear in stages instead of all at once. In very young infants, the only symptoms may be irritability, decreased activity, and trouble breathing. RSV can also cause more severe infections, especially in people at high risk. These infections include bronchiolitis, an inflammation of the small airways in the lung, and pneumonia, an infection of the lungs. If symptoms get worse over time, see a doctor right away.

plain_text:
A doctor can diagnose RSV. They can do tests such as X-rays
and blood or urine tests to check for complications in people
with severe infections. A doctor can also order lab tests, but
they are usually for people with severe infections.
